manual.title: 3x CLI and Format Reference
manual.subtitle: Commands, fields, content shapes, and automation behavior
manual.description: The exact interface for authoring and generating 3x manuals. Return to the [scheme guide](index.html) for the underlying method.
manual.footer: 3x Documentation Scheme {{project.version}} · CLI and source-format reference

sections.title: CLI Commands
sections.description: Run every command from the repository root with Python 3.9 or newer.

entries.title: init
entries.summary: Create a new manual source with the required structure and visible writing prompts.
entries.what: Writes an editable JSON source containing project metadata, theme defaults, one section, and one entry. Its triad contains unfinished-writing prompts and therefore does not pass validation until adapted.
how: `--name` sets the project name and derives a starter entry ID.
`--force` permits intentional replacement of an existing target.
entries.why: A complete structural example is faster and less error-prone than starting from an empty file. Deliberately failing prompts prevent the scaffold from being mistaken for finished documentation.

entries.title: check
entries.summary: Validate a source without creating an output artifact.
entries.what: Reports structural errors and quality warnings, prints coverage counts, and exits nonzero when errors exist.
entries.how: The command loads JSON, applies overrides, resolves placeholders, validates the complete model, and writes diagnostics to standard error. A successful summary is written to standard output.
entries.why: A read-only validation command fits editor hooks, pre-commit checks, and CI without creating generated-file churn.

entries.title: build
entries.summary: Validate and render a standalone HTML manual.
entries.synopsis: python3 scripts/manual.py build SOURCE [--output FILE] [--set PATH=VALUE ...]
entries.what: Creates the requested HTML file only when the prepared source has no validation errors. The default output is `manual.html`.
entries.how: After validation, the renderer escapes source text, applies safe inline formatting, embeds presentation and search behavior, creates parent directories as needed, and writes one UTF-8 file.
entries.why: Validation-before-write prevents a failed build from presenting a newly generated incomplete artifact as current documentation.

entries.title: watch
entries.summary: Rebuild whenever the source file changes.
entries.synopsis: python3 scripts/manual.py watch SOURCE [--output FILE] [--set PATH=VALUE ...]
entries.what: Monitors the source modification time, performs an initial build, and repeats the build after each saved change until interrupted.
entries.how: A small polling loop checks the file twice per second. If the source temporarily disappears during an editor's atomic save, the command waits for it to return.
entries.why: Fast feedback makes structural writing and visual review feel like one task while retaining a zero-dependency implementation.

sections.title: Source Format
sections.description: The JSON Schema is authoritative; these entries explain how its pieces are intended to be used.

entries.title: Root and metadata fields
entries.summary: A manual combines project identity, document identity, optional theme values, and sections.
entries.what: Defines the top-level `project`, `manual`, `theme`, and `sections` values. An optional `$schema` field lets compatible editors locate the contract.
how: `project` requires `name` and `version` and may contain other scalar placeholder values.
`theme` may set six-digit `accent` and `accent_secondary` colors plus a short `icon`.
entries.why: Separating project identity from document metadata supports multiple manuals for one project and keeps release values reusable.

entries.title: Section fields
entries.summary: Sections create ordered navigation groups around reader-oriented concepts.
entries.what: Each section requires a stable `id`, a `title`, and at least one `entry`. It may include a short `description`.
entries.how: IDs use lowercase kebab-case and share one namespace with entry IDs. Array order controls both sidebar and document order.
entries.why: Stable identifiers make links durable while explicit order lets authors teach a subject progressively rather than accepting an alphabetical or filesystem-derived sequence.

entries.title: Entry fields
entries.summary: Entries hold one documented subject and its complete 3x explanation.
entries.what: Requires `id`, `title`, `what`, `how`, and `why`. Optional fields are `summary`, `synopsis`, `tags`, `evidence`, and `related`.
how: Use `summary` for the one-sentence orientation shown before the triad.
Use `synopsis` for a literal command, API, signature, or compact contract.
Use `tags` for filtering vocabulary and `evidence` for supporting targets.
Use `related` to list stable entry IDs in reading order.
entries.why: The required core guarantees a useful minimum. Optional context supports discovery and verification without making every subject pretend to be a command or source-code component.

entries.title: What, How, and Why shapes
entries.summary: A dimension can be prose, ordered points, or a lead paragraph followed by points.
entries.what: Accepts a nonempty string, a nonempty array of strings, or an object containing `lead`, `points`, or both.
entries.how: Strings render as paragraphs. Arrays render as ordered lists. Objects render `lead` as a paragraph and `points` as an ordered list.
entries.why: A small set of semantic shapes covers most technical explanations while remaining predictable for validation, transformation, and agent generation.

entries.title: Evidence and related fields
entries.summary: Evidence records provenance; related IDs create lateral navigation.
entries.what: Evidence accepts either a target string or an object with `label` and `target`. Related accepts an array of entry IDs.
entries.how: Local evidence targets render as code-like paths and HTTP targets render as links. Related IDs resolve to entry titles and local anchors; unknown IDs produce warnings.
entries.why: Keeping provenance structured enables future renderers and audits while allowing concise input for the common file-path case.

sections.title: Processing Rules
sections.description: Preparation is deterministic: overrides, placeholders, validation, then rendering.

entries.title: Overrides and placeholders
entries.summary: Scalar configuration can flow from source metadata or the build command.
entries.what: Overrides existing dotted paths and resolves double-braced dotted-path placeholders in all strings.
entries.how: Values that parse as JSON scalars retain their types; other values remain strings. Paths must already exist, placeholders must resolve to scalars, and unknown paths stop processing.
entries.why: Existing-path enforcement catches spelling mistakes and prevents command-line options from silently inventing configuration the schema does not describe.

entries.title: Errors and warnings
entries.summary: Errors reject the document; warnings flag concerns that still need contextual judgment.
entries.what: Treats invalid JSON, missing required values, unknown fields, malformed IDs, duplicate IDs, invalid content shapes, empty dimensions, and recognized writing placeholders as errors. Missing evidence and unknown related IDs are warnings.
entries.how: Diagnostics include a JSON-like location so authors and agents can identify the affected section, entry, or field. The process exits with status one when errors exist.
entries.why: A deterministic validity boundary makes automation dependable, while warnings keep nonmechanical quality issues visible without blocking early discovery work.

entries.title: Safe inline notation
entries.summary: A deliberately small formatting vocabulary improves readability without accepting raw HTML.
entries.what: Supports backticks for code, double asterisks for strong text, single asterisks for emphasis, and Markdown-style links to HTTP, email, relative, or local-anchor targets.
entries.how: The renderer escapes source text first, recognizes only the supported patterns, validates link schemes or relative paths, and leaves unsupported markup visible as text.
entries.why: Restricting markup keeps generated manuals portable and reduces injection risk while preserving the inline conventions technical authors use most often.

entries.title: Generated output contract
entries.summary: HTML is a disposable artifact; JSON remains the source of truth.
entries.what: Emits semantic headings, stable anchors, sidebar navigation, client-side search, responsive layouts, evidence details, related links, and print rules in one file.
entries.how: CSS and a small search script are embedded. Content remains usable without a server or network connection, and narrow screens stack triad columns into a single reading flow.
entries.why: Treating HTML as generated prevents hand edits from diverging from machine-readable content and makes alternate renderers possible later.
